title: Zotter — Living by Chocolate
author_source: Mukti Khaire, Stefan Aichinger, Monika Hoffmann, Maximilian Schnoedl; Harvard Business School case 9-810-091; Feb 2010, rev. 23 Jun 2011; field case
note: The only HBS case found on an Austrian food brand. Josef Zotter (Riegersburg, Styria) after his bankruptcy in 1997 rebuilt the firm around a founder-led, 'inside-out' hand-scooped chocolate brand, organic and Fairtrade, launching up to ~90 new varieties a year without market testing. The decision point is growth: a new flagship store in Essen (Germany), further stores, and how far the brand can be stretched. The case reports that consumers did not really understand the production difference but valued the taste experience. That makes it a good audit question: what drives brand equity, product or story? Useful as a contrast case to Manner (heritage mass brand vs. founder-led craft brand).
course_use: Brand inventory and exploratory session: students map the brand elements and associations Zotter controls vs. those it cannot control, then judge the growth options. Paid via HBP (usual HBP academic price, approx. USD 4–9 per copy). Check whether WU holds a coursepack licence. The HBP product page did not render for us; case number and authors were confirmed via a library catalogue record and a copy of the case.

title: Zotter Chocolate: Creating a Market in China
author_source: Shameen Prashantham, Liman Zhao; CEIBS (China Europe International Business School) case ENT-18-538 (ENT-18-538-CE); 1 Oct 2018; 18 pp.
note: Follow-up case to the HBS Zotter case: a small Austrian family brand picks China over the US, enters through a Shanghai partner, and opens an experiential 'Chocolate Theatre' factory run by Julia Zotter. It ends in Aug 2017 with open questions about Zotter China's next steps. The brand-audit angle is whether an origin- and craft-based brand transfers to a market with low chocolate consumption and health concerns, and which associations to stress (Austrian origin, organic, experience). CEIBS also used it in its 'Real Situation Learning' with a site visit.
course_use: International brand audit, 1 session (18 pp.): pair with the HBS Zotter case for a home vs. host market brand-equity comparison. Paid; distributed by CEIBS (also check The Case Centre listing). WU licence: check.

title: Swarovski: How to shine through stormy weather?
author_source: Niccolò Pisani, Stéphane J. G. Girod; IMD case IMD-7-2430; Jan 2023; 15 pp.; teaching note available
note: The case itself, not the Nasard interview already in the guide. Swarovski's first external CEO, Alexis Nasard, takes over in July 2022 after his predecessor Robert Buchbauer resigned over disagreements with the family board. Costume jewellery is squeezed in mid-range luxury and large stores lose relevance as digital grows. Learning objectives explicitly include a SWOT and 'strategies to strengthen Swarovski's brand image'. A teaching note is listed. Works well with the Lippincott relaunch example (2021) as the brand-side evidence.
course_use: Brand audit with a strategic decision: students do the SWOT and brand-image diagnosis, then prioritise initiatives as Nasard (1 session). Paid via The Case Centre / HBP / Asia Pacific Case Center, approx. GBP/USD 5–10 per copy academic. Check WU licence.

title: Swarovski's Crystals
author_source: ICMR / IBS Case Development Centre (India); case code BSTA124; 2005; 10 pp.; compiled from published sources; no teaching note
note: Older, short case on an earlier Swarovski brand renewal. Sixth-generation family member Nadja Swarovski tries to give the swan brand a new image by extending into chandeliers and diamonds (joint venture Signity). Useful as the 'before' point in a longitudinal Swarovski brand audit: 2005 brand extension, then the 2021 Lippincott relaunch, then the 2023 IMD case. It is built only from secondary data, so it is weaker than the IMD case.
course_use: Optional pre-reading for brand extension fit / brand stretch. Cheap: Rs. 300 electronic. No teaching note.

title: Raiffeisen's Business Strategy in Russia
author_source: S. Chaudhuri, J. Chakraborty; IBS Case Development Centre (India); case code GGL0072IRC; 2010; no teaching note
note: The only teaching case found on Raiffeisen. No brand case exists in HBS, Ivey, IMD, INSEAD or LBS listings that we could find. It covers the strategy of the 2006 acquisition of Impexbank (USD 550m), not branding. It still matters for a brand audit: RBI's large Russian exposure became its main reputational and brand risk after 2022. Students can trace how a 2006 growth decision turns into a brand-reputation liability. Sister case: 'Raiffeisen's Strategic Dilemma in Ukraine' (GGL0073IRC, 2010).
course_use: Background reading only, if a team audits Raiffeisen/RBI. Use together with the RBI 2023 brand refresh and the EBI brand-value series. Paid (IBS price not shown). Low priority.

title: Kotler, Reischl & Schlader: Essentials of Modern Marketing — Edition Austria, Switzerland & Liechtenstein (local case studies incl. ÖBB)
author_source: Philip Kotler, Birgit Anna Reischl, Julia Schlader; regional edition presented at FHWien der WKW on 30 Jan 2025; contains local DACH case studies (FHWien page names Ankerbrot, Casinos Austria, ÖBB; FHWien case by Melanie Gratzer & David Dobrowsky)
note: The closest thing to a textbook case collection on Austrian brands. The FHWien announcement says it includes cases on well-known national brands such as Ankerbrot, Casinos Austria and ÖBB, plus chapters on branding and brand management. A video summary (unofficial) mentions 24 local cases. Exact case titles, length and depth were not visible online, so check the table of contents before assigning it.
course_use: Check library/WU access to the book. If the ÖBB case covers brand positioning, use it as the Austrian textbook anchor for the ÖBB examples below. Paid (book).

title: Marketagent BRAND.Diamonds 2024: Österreichs Markenstars (Manner, SPAR, EUROSPAR, Hofer, dm)
author_source: Marketagent (Thomas Schwabl); press charts, Feb 2025; 47 slides; mobile research app, n = 237,880 brand ratings, 1,266 brands, Austrian population 14+, fieldwork 01.01.–31.12.2024
note: The best free brand-tracking dataset for Austrian brands. It reports top-10 lists on 11 brand-equity questions: awareness, closeness, attraction, emotionality, fascination, connectedness ('Verbundenheit'), being 'seen with the brand', 14 personality traits, recommendation (NPS-style), distinctiveness, brand lifecycle 'season', and 'would miss it'. Manner ranks #1 in attraction (84.5% top-2-box) and #2 in emotionality (73.5%), and leads 'seen with the brand'. SPAR is #4 in connectedness (70.9%) and EUROSPAR, SPAR and Hofer appear in GenZ connectedness. Each list shows top, average and bottom values, so students can benchmark a brand against the market norm.
course_use: Data exhibit for the brand audit (exploratory part): students read the Manner and SPAR profiles across the dimensions and turn them into CBBE pyramid levels. Free PDF.

title: Marketagent BRAND.Swipe: Die authentischsten Marken Österreichs (2020)
author_source: Marketagent; BRAND.Swipe study, Nov 2020; 8 pp.; 1,396 brands; fieldwork 01.01.–08.11.2020
note: Top-20 authenticity ranking from 1,396 brands. Search coverage reports Manner as #1. Marketagent's sympathy ranking also had Manner #1 in 2018–2019 (index 85.1 in 2019), before dm took over in 2022 (Manner #3). Together with BRAND.Diamonds 2024 this gives a short time series for Manner's brand strength, useful for 'is the heritage brand still gaining?' discussions.
course_use: Second data point for a Manner or SPAR audit (trend over time). Free PDF.

title: Josef Manner & Comp. AG: Geschäftsbericht 2019 (brand portfolio and marketing section)
author_source: Josef Manner & Comp. AG (listed on Vienna Stock Exchange); annual report 2019; 58 pp.; PDF
note: Primary source for a Manner brand inventory. The marketing section covers the portfolio (Manner, Casali, Napoli/Dragee Keksi, Victor Schmidt/Mozartkugeln, Ildefonso) and new flavours aimed at 'Neuverwender, insbesondere jüngere Zielgruppen'. It also covers Victor Schmidt's 110th anniversary, the 'Rosa macht glücklich' advertising line, the website relaunch, #pinkplayground, and awards (e.g. Marketagent 2019: most-liked brand ahead of Wikipedia and dm). It includes key figures 2015–2019. Because Manner is listed, newer annual reports are on josef.manner.com, e.g. 2024 revenue approx. EUR 288m.
course_use: Brand inventory exercise: students extract brand elements, sub-brands and marketing activities from the report, then compare with the consumer data (BRAND.Diamonds). Free.

title: Manner Vollkornschnitte: Platin-Effie 2013 (and Manner personalised packs: Effie Gold + Platin)
author_source: IAA Austria Effie Awards 2013, reported by Leadersnet; client Josef Manner & Comp AG; agencies Demner, Merlicek & Bergmann (creative), OMD (media)
note: Documented brand-extension result with numbers. The wholegrain wafer, positioned as a 'sweet alternative', won the Platinum Effie (Food). Sales grew +9.9% in 2012, about ten times faster than the confectionery market, with ~0.75 kg sold per EUR 1 of advertising and a repurchase rate of 63.6%. A later Manner case with personalised packaging (in-house creative, OMD media) won Gold and the Platinum Effie again (Der Standard, 'Wirksamste Werbeschnitte', https://www.derstandard.at/2000067718868/; seen in search results only). The same Leadersnet page lists the ÖBB ÖSTERREICHcard among the 2013 winners.
course_use: Discussion: does a health-oriented line extension strengthen or dilute the core Manner associations? Use the Effie KPIs as 'outcome' evidence in the audit. Free.

title: Origin as brand essence: Manner and Almdudler as case companies (NHH master thesis, 2012)
author_source: Master thesis, NHH Norwegian School of Economics, 2012; NHH Brage open-access repository
note: Qualitative study of Josef Manner & Comp AG and Almdudler. Finding: both use their Austrian/Viennese origin not as a secondary association but as an essential part of the brand. A useful academic frame for the 'secondary associations / country of origin' part of a Manner audit. We did not open the full text: the repository host did not resolve, so authors and exact title are not verified.
course_use: Optional reading for student teams auditing Manner or Almdudler. Free (open access) if the link resolves; otherwise search NHH Brage for 'Manner Almdudler'.

title: Rauch: neues Dachmarken-Bild 'Rauch-Baum' und internationaler Etat an Wensauer & Partner (2009)
author_source: HORIZONT Online, 7 Apr 2009
note: One of the few documented brand-architecture moves by Rauch. After a pitch, Wensauer & Partner took on international communication, and the first output was a new umbrella-brand image built on the 'Rauch-Baum' (tree), described as standing for 'frischeste Fruchtkompetenz des Unternehmens und der Dachmarke Rauch'. Rauch at the time: 2008 revenue EUR 720m, exports to 90+ countries, brands Bravo, Happy Day, Ice Tea, Nativa. No teaching case on Rauch exists in the case databases we searched (Case Centre, HBP, Ivey, IMD). This plus the items below is the best available material for a house-of-brands vs. umbrella-brand discussion.
course_use: Brand architecture mini-exercise: draw the Rauch portfolio (Rauch, Happy Day, Bravo, Rauch Eistee, Yippy, Nativa, Franz Josef Rauch, Kloster Kitchen acquired 2024/25) and judge the role of the umbrella brand. Free.

title: Rauch Happy Day: Packaging-Relaunch der 1-Liter-Range (2018)
author_source: about-drinks.com, 22 Oct 2018 (press release Rauch Deutschland); plus Rauch '100 x Rauch 1919–2019' company history
note: Packaging as the key brand touchpoint for Rauch. The 2018 Happy Day 1-l Tetra Pak redesign (new flavour bands, colours, pure fruit imagery, icons on the back) aimed at shelf impact, impulse purchase and repurchase in German retail (Rauch 2017 revenue EUR 902m). The company history page https://www.rauch.cc/company/100-x-rauch-1919-2019/posts/standing-out-on-supermarket-shelves documents the 2001 glass bottle for gastronomy and the 2006–07 PET bottle with the embossed Rauch ellipse as the brand's distinctive asset. Good for a distinctive-asset audit.
course_use: Distinctive brand assets exercise: which Rauch/Happy Day codes (ellipse, tree, colours) are distinctive and owned? Students check shelf photos against the brand guidelines. Free.

title: RBI launches new group brand design and slogan 'Make it happen' (2023)
author_source: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Group Communications; press release, 8 May 2023
note: Documented brand-architecture harmonisation across RBI's CEE network banks. Head of Group Marketing: 'Up until now, the only unifying elements across the Group were the iconic gable cross and distinctive yellow.' Changes: brand strategy, architecture and identity harmonised; brand idea 'Ease'; slogan 'Make it happen'. FutureBrand London (branding) and McCann Bucharest (creative) were chosen after two pitches, and the launch included a metaverse pavilion. Contrast: the Austrian Raiffeisen Bankengruppe (cooperative, regional banks, Landesbanken) keeps its own claim 'WIR macht's möglich'. This is a live example of one brand name under two architectures.
course_use: Brand architecture discussion: who owns 'Raiffeisen'? Map RBI vs. Raiffeisen Bankengruppe Österreich vs. Raiffeisen Schweiz (separate rebrand by MetaDesign). Free.

title: FutureBrand: Raiffeisen Bank International brand strategy, architecture and identity
author_source: FutureBrand (agency case page), c. 2023
note: Agency view of the RBI repositioning. The challenge: move from a 'trusted but conventional network bank' to a more emotive, innovative brand that stands out against legacy banks and fintechs. The new architecture links segments, products and initiatives, aiming to attract tech-savvy newcomers and keep high-value customers. The Gable Cross and yellow were kept as equity assets, and new 'brand arrows' and a sonic identity were added. No results or metrics are reported, which is itself a good audit discussion point.
course_use: Pair with the RBI press release: students identify which equity elements were kept vs. replaced, and what tracking they would require to evaluate it. Free.

title: Raiffeisen Bankengruppe Österreich: Giebelkreuz, Struktur und Markenversprechen (Selbstdarstellung)
author_source: raiffeisen.at, 'Die Raiffeisen Bankengruppe' (accessed Oct 2026)
note: Primary source for the brand inventory of the Austrian group. It describes a three-tier structure (Raiffeisenbanken, Raiffeisenlandesbanken, RBI) plus specialised companies (Capital Management, Versicherung, Leasing, Bausparkasse). It reports 1,500+ branches, approx. 4.4 million customers and 26,800 employees, and frames members as co-owners. The Giebelkreuz and name 'stehen für Sicherheit und verlässliche Partnerschaft', with brand pillars 'Raiffeisen ist sicher / regional / Alles aus einer Hand'. Regional pages add the claim 'WIR macht's möglich' and the founder quote 'Was dem Einzelnen nicht möglich ist, das vermögen viele'.
course_use: Brand inventory: students compare the intended brand (this page) with external data (EBI brand values, reputation rankings, the Russia debate). Free.

title: Markenwertstudie 2012 (European Brand Institute): Raiffeisen −22.6%, Erste −31.4%, ÖBB +10%
author_source: Leadersnet report on the 9th Austrian brand value study by the European Brand Institute (Gerhard Hrebicek), 2012
note: Historical counterpoint to the EBI 2026 study already in the guide. Top 10 with 2011→2012 values: Raiffeisen fell from rank 3 to 5 (EUR 2.94bn → 2.28bn, attributed to scandals). Erste Bank dropped 31.4% to rank 9, while ÖBB gained ~10% (EUR 1.38bn → 1.52bn) and Spar was stable at rank 7 (+2%). Later EBI waves show Raiffeisen stuck around rank 7 (~EUR 2.04bn in 2024) while Erste rose to #3 in 2026. This gives a 14-year brand-value trajectory for three of the five target brands.
course_use: Outcome-metric exercise: why did bank brand values fall in 2012, and what does a financial brand valuation capture that consumer tracking (BRAND.Diamonds) does not? Free.

title: ÖBB: neue Markenstrategie, Positionierung und Arbeitgebermarke — 'Heute. Für morgen. Für uns.' (2019)
author_source: Leadersnet, 2 Oct 2019; client ÖBB Holding AG (Corporate Communications, Senior Brand Management); AANDRS (creation), Brainds (strategic brand development and brand design), ÖBB Werbung (in-house)
note: The best-documented ÖBB repositioning. After a multi-year internal culture programme, ÖBB moved from fixed testimonials to 'real people'. It positioned itself as 'die sinnvollste Lösung für Mensch, Umwelt und Wirtschaft' (climate and sustainable mobility) with the claim 'Heute. Für morgen. Für uns.' It extracted the red 'Raute' from the Ö-stroke of the wordmark as a distinctive asset, and launched the employer brand 'Jobs mit Sinn', driven by a quarter of staff retiring. No tracking data are given, but ÖBB is one of few Austrian brands whose EBI brand value rose sharply (+10% in 2012).
course_use: Example of a corporate + employer brand repositioning for a state-owned brand: students write the positioning statement and propose audit KPIs (image, consideration, employer attractiveness). Free.

title: ÖBB Dachkampagne 'Jede Fahrt macht den Unterschied' (2022)
author_source: Leadersnet, 21 Aug 2022; creation Ortner&Weihs; development ÖBB Werbung (in-house); music Wiener Symphoniker
note: Next step of the 2019 repositioning. ÖBB presents itself as 'one of Austria's largest climate-protection companies' and targets undecided non-users while affirming existing customers. The 360° campaign ran across TV, cinema, OOH, print wraps and ÖBB Railscreens. Together with the 2019 article it shows brand consistency over time (same claim and red, a new narrative), useful for checking consistency in an audit.
course_use: Consistency check over two campaign waves (2019 → 2022). Free.

title: SPAR Food-Salon 2026: Eigenmarken-Architektur (S-BUDGET, Natur*pur, Vital) und Marktanteil
author_source: Leadersnet, 26 Apr 2026 (Markus Kaser, deputy CEO SPAR Österreich)
note: Current figures on SPAR's private-label brand architecture: approx. 10,000 own-brand items and ~45% of revenue. S-BUDGET has approx. EUR 1bn revenue in Austria, 1,100+ products and +8%. SPAR Natur*pur is 30 years old with +8.7%, and SPAR Vital grew +15%. Market share was 36.2% at end of 2025 (NielsenIQ, after a 0.6-point correction). Also covers dropping the online grocery shop and the 'shrinkflation' positioning against branded manufacturers. No teaching case on SPAR Austria exists in the major case databases. This and the next row are the best documented brand-strategy data.
course_use: Retailer brand portfolio audit: map the good-better-best tiers (S-BUDGET / SPAR / SPAR Premium) plus benefit lines (Natur*pur, Vital, Veggie) and judge overlaps and gaps. Free.

title: Eigenmarken treiben Wachstum: Spar vergrößert Abstand zur Konkurrenz (Ergebnisse 2025)
author_source: VOL.AT / APA, 13 Mar 2026; market data NielsenIQ via 'Key Account' (Feb 2026)
note: Market-outcome data for a SPAR audit. Austrian market shares 2025: SPAR 36.8%, REWE (Billa, Penny) 32.3%, Hofer + Lidl 25.5%. SPAR Austria store revenue +4.2% to EUR 10.8bn, group EUR 22.3bn, S-BUDGET +8%, Unimarkt takeover (+0.2 pp). Earlier coverage (2024 results) gives tier growth: S-BUDGET +8.5%, SPAR Premium +11%, Natur*pur +8%, Veggie +13%, and own-brand share up from 25% (2007) to 45%. Combine with BRAND.Diamonds (SPAR #4 in connectedness) for the consumer side.
course_use: Link the brand-equity data (BRAND.Diamonds) with market outcomes (share, own-brand growth). Free.

title: Erste Group: '...and then there was George' — launch of the George digital banking brand (2015)
author_source: Erste Group press release, Jan 2015; INTEGRAL online survey, n = 900 Austrians 16+, fieldwork 21–30 Nov 2014
note: Rare example of a brand launch justified with published consumer research. Comparisons of banks vs. tech platforms: 81% find their bank trustworthy vs. 3% for Facebook, 74% vs. 1% for Google on data safety, and 45% enjoy Facebook vs. 18% online banking. 80–94% would not buy financial products from Amazon, Google or Facebook. The naming rationale ties George to the early 'Let George do it' autopilot, giving the brand personality. George later reached 1m users in Austria and was rolled out across Erste's CEE markets. Erste is now #3 in EBI 2026 (+26.6%).
course_use: Show how a points-of-parity / points-of-difference argument (trust vs. ease and design) is built from survey data, then ask students what tracking would show whether George strengthened or diluted the Erste/Sparkasse brand. Free.

title: Swarovski brand relaunch with Lippincott: 'making crystal cool again' (2021)
author_source: Lippincott (agency case page); relaunch Feb 2021; logo redesign led in-house by creative director Giovanna Engelbert
note: Agency case with an explicit audit finding: Swarovski was perceived as near-luxury but had trained customers to expect entry-level prices and discounts, so the brand was eroding its own image. Response: a bolder brand platform, new product range, higher average price point, new logo (swan turned around), the 'Instant Wonder' concept store in Milan, plans for 28 more stores, and an internal engagement campaign. The page cites WWD: strongest growth in seven years, retail sales +13%, B2B crystal +5%. Complements the IMD case and the Nasard interview already in the guide.
course_use: Before/after audit: students reconstruct the 'as-is' brand image from the diagnosis and test whether the relaunch closes the gap to the intended identity. Free.

title: Austrian Airlines further develops its branding for the digital age (2018)
author_source: GTP Headlines, 20 Apr 2018 (Austrian Airlines announcement; CCO Andreas Otto)
note: Evolutionary rebrand of a national-flag brand inside the Lufthansa Group. Chevron and 'Austrian' wordmark modernised for legibility on smartphones and smartwatches and at distance on aircraft. Signature red used more deliberately as the differentiator, 'Servus' kept on the belly. Gradual livery rollout (18 of 82 aircraft by summer 2019, about seven years for the full fleet). The earlier 2015 'red-white-red' change dropped the sky blue after the Tyrolean merger. A good case for 'evolution vs. revolution' and the cost and timing of brand changes.
course_use: Discussion on retaining brand elements: which equities (red, chevron, 'Servus') must be kept, and how a digital-first brief changes logo design. Free.

title: BIPA: neuer Markenauftritt 'Alles beginnt mit einem großen B' (2026)
author_source: Leadersnet, 21 Jan 2026; BIPA (REWE International), MD Markus Geyer; BBDO Wien (corporate design), AANDRS (campaign)
note: Repeated repositioning of an Austrian drugstore brand against dm. In 2017 Serviceplan repositioned BIPA with 'Weil ich ein Mädchen bin' (tone, look, range and store layout; Der Standard, seen in search results only). The 2026 relaunch makes the letter 'B' the key visual and adds the tagline 'Wir sind da, für das, was das Leben bringt'. It also brings reduced design, real people, and new store entrances and wayfinding. No research data are cited. Marketagent data place dm among Austria's most-liked brands, the obvious benchmark.
course_use: Challenger vs. leader audit: BIPA vs. dm, using Marketagent data for dm and the two repositionings (2017, 2026) to discuss consistency. Free.

title: Kitzbühel Tourismus zieht Rebranding-Bilanz (one year after the relaunch)
author_source: Leadersnet, 23 Jun 2025 (relaunch 20 Jun 2024)
note: Austrian destination rebrand with a post-launch review. Changes: first new logo in 50 years, a fashion-like design that moved toward 'Artificial Design', and rights secured to Alfons Walde's original 'Gams' after three years of negotiation. Reported measures: campaign reach 54m, press reach 87m, and effectiveness tests at Sporthochschule Köln (eye-tracking, recall, in-depth interviews) showing higher attractiveness, sympathy, visit intent and recommendation among those exposed. Exact figures are not given. German Design Award 2025.
course_use: Use to discuss what a credible post-rebrand audit should contain (baseline, control group, exact KPIs) versus what is reported here. Free.

title: Stiegl: 'Stiegl und stolz drauf' brand relaunch (2022)
author_source: Wien Nord Serviceplan / House of Communication (agency case page); launch reported by Leadersnet, 16 May 2022
note: Agency case with an explicit audit diagnosis: Stiegl's image was 'fragmented by too many campaigns and TV spots, with no consistent brand codes'. The market is dominated by Heineken/Brau Union. The response was one central idea for Austria's largest private brewery (founded 1492): raising a glass as a gesture of respect, 'the beer of all Austrians'. It serves as an umbrella for brand, product, employer branding and sponsorship. No KPIs are reported. Leadersnet launch article: https://www.leadersnet.at/news/59010,stiegl-launcht-neuen-markenauftritt-und-ist-stolz-drauf.html
course_use: Shows the typical audit outcome 'inconsistent brand codes' and its remedy. Students can audit Stiegl's current touchpoints for consistency. Free.

title: Hofer 'Austropop' / Hofer Song 2020 image campaign
author_source: Ogilvy Austria (agency case page); client Hofer KG; Staatspreis Werbung
note: Discounter brand-image campaign with an explicit brand objective: strengthen price perception and exclusive own brands, celebrate diverse customers, and offer distraction during the pandemic. It was a 360° campaign (radio, Spotify, YouTube, TikTok, OOH) and won the Staatspreis Werbung. No KPIs are given. Useful alongside the SPAR rows for comparing how competing grocers build own-brand equity.
course_use: Grocery brand comparison (SPAR vs. Hofer vs. BILLA): positioning maps and own-brand roles. Free.
